drivingQuestion: Which tanna is the author of the mishna's 5/6/7 with permission to add?
outcomeNote: The question is left open here and taken up in the next unit (Rava: the school of R' Yishmael)

segments.he: בְּיוֹם טוֹב חֲמִשָּׁה, בְּיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים שִׁשָּׁה כּוּ׳. מַתְנִיתִין מַנִּי? לֹא רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל וְלָא רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא. דְּתַנְיָא: בְּיוֹם טוֹב חֲמִשָּׁה, וּבְיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים שִׁשָּׁה, וּבְשַׁבָּת שִׁבְעָה, אֵין פּוֹחֲתִין מֵהֶן וְאֵין מוֹסִיפִין עֲלֵיהֶן, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל. רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: בְּיוֹם טוֹב חֲמִשָּׁה, וּבְיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים שִׁבְעָה, וּבְשַׁבָּת שִׁשָּׁה, אֵין פּוֹחֲתִין מֵהֶן אֲבָל מוֹסִיפִין עֲלֵיהֶן.
segments.en: We learned in the mishna: «On a Festival, five» people read; «on Yom Kippur, six» people read; and on Shabbat, seven people read. One may not decrease the number of readers, but one may add to them. The Gemara asks: «Who is» the tanna of «the mishna?» It is «not Rabbi Yishmael and not Rabbi Akiva, as it is taught» in a baraita: «On a Festival, five» people read from the Torah; «and on Yom Kippur, six» people read; «and on Shabbat, seven» people read. «One may not decrease or add to» the required number of readers. This is «the statement of Rabbi Yishmael. Rabbi Akiva» disagrees and «says: On a Festival, five» people read from the Torah; «and on Yom Kippur, seven» people read; «and on Shabbat, six» people read. «One may not decrease» these numbers, «but one may add to them.»
